text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 2: At three wind farms, CERRA's wind has a higher error than ERA5's and NORA3's does not clearly differ'
text.tspan: Figure 2: At three wind farms, CERRA's wind has a higher error than
ERA5's and NORA3's does not clearly differ

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Top panel of each block: each arm's mean absolute error minus ERA5's. Lower panel: that block's two planned contrasts, the first arm's error minus the second's. Each arm's own error is in Figure 1. Compare arms only within a block: the blocks differ in rows, hours of the day, period, and fitted XGBoost models, and even their ERA5 rows differ, so no CERRA row is comparable with any NORA3 row. No correction is made for the number of exploratory contrasts, and the contrasts are correlated. CERRA: 0.0% of scored rows are in a calendar month, seen in two or more years, with no training row in their fold, and 4.5% are in a calendar month seen in one year only, which no fold design can cover. NORA3: 0.0% of scored rows are in a calendar month, seen in two or more years, with no training row in their fold, and 0.0% are in a calendar month seen in one year only, which no fold design can cover. Wind heights: ERA5, CERRA, and NORA3 at 100 m, the ICON products at 80 m, UKV at 100 m. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole calendar months, each with all three farms' rows, and a fitting seed. The interval does not cover variation between the three farms. Errors are a fraction of each generator's 99th-percentile output, not its nameplate capacity. Three wind farms in Lincolnshire. CERRA and NORA3 are read at 100 m. Every contrast in a top panel is against ERA5, scored on that block's own rows. Hollow triangle: the same contrast at the second hyperparameter setting, shown for planned contrasts and for contrasts near the 5% line. Planned: written into the study plan before the block's first fit, which is the new product's contrast against ERA5 and against ICON-D2. Every other row is exploratory.'
text.tspan: Top panel of each block: each arm's mean absolute error minus ERA5's. Lower panel: that block's two
planned contrasts, the first arm's error minus the second's.
Each arm's own error is in Figure 1.
Compare arms only within a block: the blocks differ in rows, hours of the day, period, and fitted
XGBoost models, and even their ERA5 rows differ, so no CERRA row is comparable with any NORA3 row.
No correction is made for the number of exploratory contrasts, and the contrasts are correlated.
CERRA: 0.0% of scored rows are in a calendar month, seen in two or more years, with no training row
in their fold, and 4.5% are in a calendar month seen in one year only, which no fold design can
cover.
NORA3: 0.0% of scored rows are in a calendar month, seen in two or more years, with no training row
in their fold, and 0.0% are in a calendar month seen in one year only, which no fold design can
cover.
Wind heights: ERA5, CERRA, and NORA3 at 100 m, the ICON products at 80 m, UKV at 100 m.
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole calendar months, each with all three farms'
rows, and a fitting seed. The interval does not cover variation between the three farms.
Errors are a fraction of each generator's 99th-percentile output, not its nameplate capacity.
Three wind farms in Lincolnshire. CERRA and NORA3 are read at 100 m.
Every contrast in a top panel is against ERA5, scored on that block's own rows.
Hollow triangle: the same contrast at the second hyperparameter setting, shown for planned contrasts and for
contrasts near the 5% line.
Planned: written into the study plan before the block's first fit, which is the new product's contrast against ERA5
and against ICON-D2. Every other row is exploratory.
